newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian insurer plans to give away over US$1 bln.
newsitem.headline: Australian insurer plans to give away over US$1 bln.

text.p: Australia's Colonial Mutual on Friday joined an emerging queue of life insurers waiting to list on the local bourse, unveiling plans to give A$1.3 billion (US$1 billion) worth of shares to its policy-holders.

Colonial said it would distribute the 500 million shares to 538,000 members in Australia, New Zealand, Britain and Fiji and raise another A$550 million before it lists on the Australian and New Zealand stock exchanges in the first half of 1997.

Chief executive Peter Smedley said the group's mutual structure, which requires it to act solely in the policy-holders' best interests, limited its ability to expand into an increasingly global financial services market.

"Demutualisation will provide Colonial with more direct access to capital markets ... and will give us flexibility to expand the business, particularly in growth markets," he told a news conference in the group's Melbourne headquarters.

Colonial, the smallest of Australia's big three mutual life insurance groups, follows the path of French-controlled National Mutual Holdings Ltd, which plans to list on the Australian and New Zealand bourses next month in a multi-billion dollar float.
The nation's largest life insurer, the Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP), has said it will consider demutualising as part of a review of is organisation structure.
AMP plans to release a decision by the end of 1996.
A total of 500 million Colonial shares, each with an appraisal value of A$2.57, will be distributed.
They will be attached to an issue of 500 million options on new ordinary shares in the group, raising A$200 million, Colonial Mutual said.

The group will raise another A$350 million from institutions through an issue of converting preference shares to help meet the cost of the demutualisation and restructuring of the group and to fund business plans of Colonial's strategic units.
Colonial also has operations in Hong Kong, the Philippines and Singapore through a joint venture with trading house Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd unit Jardine Pacific.
The insurer has also forged joint ventures with the Astra group in Indonesia, the Bank of Ayudhya group in Thailand and Edaran Otomobil Nasional in Malaysia.
